Where are those resolved from?                                                                                                                                                                                                               

⏺ Good catch — those are unresolved.

  How they resolve today: The string in screen("missions.ogre_cave.no_trace") is a dotted text id that the opaque engine looks up via res_text(id). The lookup table is registered by the strings { import("texts/missions.json5") } block near the top of the DSL. That maps onto the existing
  data/world/texts/missions.json5 shard, which has a tree like ogre_cave: { no_trace: "You search the cave but find no trace...", kastagir_note: "...", leave_cave: "..." }. There's a two-step resolver (<script_id>.<name> then strip to <parent>.<name>) so the ids work whether the script is nested under
  missions.ogre_cave or shares the parent atom.

  But: that's exactly the shape you said you wanted to move away from for mission flavour. Your instruction earlier was:

  ▎ Inline narration at a call site is appropriate where it is small or where it is unique narration in a mission. Perhaps before/after a mission encounter — that may even contain logic make a choice or go to narration a or b or whatever.

  So screen("missions.ogre_cave.no_trace") is technically faithful to the current architecture but is a placeholder, not the target shape. The target shape would be:

  mission("ogre_cave") {
      body {
          // ...
          encounter("ogre_lord", mandatory = true)
          clw()
          say("You finish the lord and search the cave.")
          say("There's no trace of Tammy — only her torn cloak,")
          say("and a folded note in a hand you don't recognise.")
          waitInput(); clw()
          say("The note reads: '...'")
          // ...
      }
  }

  I left them as ids in this pass for two reasons:
  1. The full text corpus is ~15 shards; inlining everything verbatim would have added ~1500-2000 LOC and required reading every text file to copy strings I didn't have memorised.
  2. Some shards (common.*, speak.chit.*, terrain.*) genuinely should stay referenced — they're shared across many call sites or driven by emit_indexed dispatch.

  The mission-shaped ones (missions.bandits.*, missions.ogre_cave.*, etc.) and the unique mission-bound speak scenes (speak.husband.first_visit, speak.erethor.delivered_lute, etc.) are the strong candidates for actual inlining.

  Want me to do an inlining pass over the mission and unique-speak narration — read the relevant data/world/texts/missions.json5 and texts/speak.json5 shards and replace screen("missions.X.Y") with the actual say("...") lines? That would push the file to ~4500 LOC but make mission flow read like a screenplay,
  which is what you originally described.

⏺ You're right — those .0/.1/.2 ids are a translation artifact from the JSON5 line-arrays. Kotlin can do multi-line strings. Let me collapse them.

⏺ Bash(python3 <<'PYEOF'
      import re

      src_path = '/Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts'
      src = open(src_path).read()

      # Locate strings block.
      start_marker = '    strings {\n'
      start = src.index(start_marker)
      remaining = src[start + len(start_marker):]
      end_idx = remaining.index('\n    }\n')
      old_body = remaining[:end_idx + 1]

      # Parse each line; group consecutive str("X.N", "...") with same X.
      str_re = re.compile(r'^(\s*)str\("([^"]*)", "((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"\)\s*$')
      indexed_re = re.compile(r'^(.*)\.(\d+)$')

      lines = old_body.split('\n')
      out_lines = []
      i = 0
      while i < len(lines):
          line = lines[i]
          m = str_re.match(line)
          if not m:
              out_lines.append(line); i += 1; continue
          indent, full_id, value = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
          im = indexed_re.match(full_id)
          if not im or int(im.group(2)) != 0:
              # Plain (non-indexed) or starts at non-zero -- emit unchanged.
              out_lines.append(line); i += 1; continue
          base_id = im.group(1)
          # Collect consecutive .0, .1, .2, ...
          parts = [value]
          j = i + 1
          n = 1
          while j < len(lines):
              m2 = str_re.match(lines[j])
              if not m2: break
              full_id2 = m2.group(2)
              im2 = indexed_re.match(full_id2)
              if not im2 or im2.group(1) != base_id: break
              if int(im2.group(2)) != n: break
              parts.append(m2.group(3))
              n += 1; j += 1
          if len(parts) == 1:
              # Single-element array -> drop the .0 suffix.
              out_lines.append(f'{indent}str("{base_id}", "{parts[0]}")')
          else:
              # Join with \n. Trailing empty parts become trailing \n.
              joined = '\\n'.join(parts)
              out_lines.append(f'{indent}str("{base_id}", "{joined}")')
          i = j

      new_body = '\n'.join(out_lines)
      new_src = src[:start + len(start_marker)] + new_body + src[start + len(start_marker) + end_idx + 1:]
      open(src_path, 'w').write(new_src)

      # Quick stats.
      old_str_count = sum(1 for l in lines if str_re.match(l))
      new_str_count = sum(1 for l in out_lines if str_re.match(l))
      print(f'str count: {old_str_count} -> {new_str_count}')
      print(f'block lines: {len(lines)} -> {len(out_lines)}')
      PYEOF
      wc -l /Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts)

⏺ Clean: no \\ or \" escapes, 523 multi-line entries. Let me convert.

⏺ Bash(python3 <<'PYEOF'
      import re

      src_path = '/Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts'
      src = open(src_path).read()

      start_marker = '    strings {\n'
      start = src.index(start_marker)
      remaining = src[start + len(start_marker):]
      end_idx = remaining.index('\n    }\n')
      old_body = remaining[:end_idx + 1]

      str_re = re.compile(r'^(\s*)str\("([^"]*)", "((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"\)\s*$')

      lines = old_body.split('\n')
      out_lines = []
      converted = 0
      for line in lines:
          m = str_re.match(line)
          if not m:
              out_lines.append(line); continue
          indent, sid, value = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
          if r'\n' not in value:
              out_lines.append(line); continue
          # Multi-line: emit triple-quoted with trimIndent.
          # Split on literal `\n` (escape sequence in the source).
          parts = value.split(r'\n')
          inner_indent = indent + '    '
          body_lines = []
          for p in parts:
              # No \" or \\ in the data (verified) -- can paste raw.
              body_lines.append(inner_indent + p if p else '')
          body = '\n'.join(body_lines)
          out_lines.append(f'{indent}str("{sid}", """')
          out_lines.append(body)
          out_lines.append(f'{indent}""".trimIndent())')
          converted += 1

      new_body = '\n'.join(out_lines)
      new_src = src[:start + len(start_marker)] + new_body + src[start + len(start_marker) + end_idx + 1:]
      open(src_path, 'w').write(new_src)

      import re
      from collections import defaultdict, OrderedDict

      src_path = '/Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts'
      src = open(src_path).read()

      start_marker = '    strings {\n'
      start = src.index(start_marker)
      remaining = src[start + len(start_marker):]
      end_idx = remaining.index('\n    }\n')
      old_body = remaining[:end_idx + 1]

      lines = old_body.split('\n')

      single_re = re.compile(r'^(\s+)str\("([^"]+)", "((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"\)\s*$')
      multi_open_re = re.compile(r'^(\s+)str\("([^"]+)", """\s*$')
      shard_comment_re = re.compile(r'^\s*//\s*-+\s*([a-z_]+)\.json5\s*-+\s*$')

      # Walk lines preserving order; emit a list of entries (id -> body) and
      # remember which "shard" they belong to (from comment headers). We will
      # regroup by parent prefix within shard.
      shard_of_entry = []  # parallel to entries
      entries = []  # (id, body_lines_or_scalar, is_multi)
      current_shard = None

      i = 0
      while i < len(lines):
          line = lines[i]
          cm = shard_comment_re.match(line)
          if cm:
              current_shard = cm.group(1)
              i += 1; continue
          m = single_re.match(line)
          if m:
              entries.append((m.group(2), m.group(3), False))
              shard_of_entry.append(current_shard)
              i += 1; continue
          m = multi_open_re.match(line)
          if m:
              indent = m.group(1)
              sid = m.group(2)
              body_lines = []
              i += 1
              close_re = re.compile(rf'^{re.escape(indent)}"""\)\s*$')
              while i < len(lines) and not close_re.match(lines[i]):
                  body_lines.append(lines[i])
                  i += 1
              i += 1
              # Strip leading + trailing blank lines (the """ boundary blanks)
              while body_lines and body_lines[0].strip() == '':
                  body_lines.pop(0)
              while body_lines and body_lines[-1].strip() == '':
                  body_lines.pop()
              # Compute and strip common indent
              non_blank = [bl for bl in body_lines if bl.strip()]
              if non_blank:
                  common = min(len(bl) - len(bl.lstrip(' ')) for bl in non_blank)
                  body_lines = [bl[common:] if bl.strip() else '' for bl in body_lines]
              entries.append((sid, body_lines, True))
              shard_of_entry.append(current_shard)
              continue
          i += 1

      # Group by parent prefix (rpartition).
      # Preserve original order of first appearance per prefix.
      prefix_order = []
      groups = OrderedDict()
      entry_shard = {}
      for (sid, body, multi), sh in zip(entries, shard_of_entry):
          if '.' in sid:
              prefix, _, tag = sid.rpartition('.')
          else:
              prefix = ''
              tag = sid
          if prefix not in groups:
              groups[prefix] = []
              entry_shard[prefix] = sh
          groups[prefix].append((tag, body, multi))

      # Emit new body. Group by shard (insert shard header comments).
      out = []
      indent = '        '
      inner = indent + '    '
      last_shard = None
      for prefix, items in groups.items():
          sh = entry_shard[prefix]
          if sh != last_shard:
              if last_shard is not None:
                  out.append('')
              out.append(f'{indent}// ----- {sh}.json5 -----')
              last_shard = sh

          if len(items) == 1:
              tag, body, multi = items[0]
              full_id = f'{prefix}.{tag}' if prefix else tag
              if multi:
                  out.append(f'{indent}str("{full_id}", """')
                  for bl in body:
                      out.append(inner + bl if bl else '')
                  out.append(f'{indent}""")')
              else:
                  # Escape any " or \ in scalar (we audited: none present)
                  out.append(f'{indent}str("{full_id}", "{body}")')
          else:
              out.append(f'{indent}screens("{prefix}", """')
              for j, (tag, body, multi) in enumerate(items):
                  if j > 0:
                      out.append('')
                  out.append(f'{inner}[{tag}]')
                  if multi:
                      for bl in body:
                          out.append(inner + bl if bl else '')
                  else:
                      out.append(f'{inner}{body}')
              out.append(f'{indent}""")')

      new_body = '\n' + '\n'.join(out) + '\n'
      new_src = src[:start + len(start_marker)] + new_body + src[start + len(start_marker) + end_idx + 1:]
      open(src_path, 'w').write(new_src)

      print(f'entries={len(entries)} groups={len(groups)} ' +
            f'screens={sum(1 for v in groups.values() if len(v)>1)} ' +
            f'singles={sum(1 for v in groups.values() if len(v)==1)}')
      PYEOF
      wc -l /Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts)

      import re

      src_path = '/Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts'
      src = open(src_path).read()

      start_marker = '    strings {\n'
      start = src.index(start_marker)
      remaining = src[start + len(start_marker):]
      end_idx = remaining.index('\n    }\n')
      old_body = remaining[:end_idx + 1]

      lines = old_body.split('\n')

      screens_open_re = re.compile(r'^(\s+)screens\("([^"]+)", """\s*$')
      str_single_re = re.compile(r'^(\s+)str\("([^"]+)", "((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"\)\s*$')
      str_multi_open_re = re.compile(r'^(\s+)str\("([^"]+)", """\s*$')
      tag_re = re.compile(r'^\s*\[([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\]\s*$')

      out = []
      indent = '        '
      inner = indent + '    '

      i = 0
      while i < len(lines):
          line = lines[i]
          m = screens_open_re.match(line)
          if not m:
              out.append(line); i += 1; continue
          prefix = m.group(2)
          # Read until closing line `        """)`
          body = []
          i += 1
          close_re = re.compile(rf'^{re.escape(m.group(1))}"""\)\s*$')
          while i < len(lines) and not close_re.match(lines[i]):
              body.append(lines[i])
              i += 1
          i += 1  # skip close line
          # Find common indent of non-blank body lines (should all be at +4)
          non_blank = [bl for bl in body if bl.strip()]
          common = min((len(bl) - len(bl.lstrip(' ')) for bl in non_blank), default=0)
          # Strip common indent
          stripped = [bl[common:] if bl.strip() else '' for bl in body]
          # Trim leading + trailing blanks
          while stripped and stripped[0].strip() == '': stripped.pop(0)
          while stripped and stripped[-1].strip() == '': stripped.pop()
          # Walk: find [tag] markers; collect lines until next tag.
          sections = []  # list of (tag, body_lines)
          cur_tag = None; cur_body = []
          for bl in stripped:
              tm = tag_re.match(bl)
              if tm:
                  if cur_tag is not None:
                      # Trim trailing blank from previous
                      while cur_body and cur_body[-1].strip() == '':
                          cur_body.pop()
                      sections.append((cur_tag, cur_body))
                  cur_tag = tm.group(1); cur_body = []
              else:
                  cur_body.append(bl)
          if cur_tag is not None:
              while cur_body and cur_body[-1].strip() == '':
                  cur_body.pop()

              if len(sec_body) == 1 and '\\' not in sec_body[0] and '"' not in sec_body[0]:
                  # Single-line scalar: keep as one-line str()
                  out.append(f'{indent}str("{full_id}", "{sec_body[0]}")')
              else:
                  out.append(f'{indent}str("{full_id}", """')
                  for bl in sec_body:
                      out.append(inner + bl if bl else '')
                  out.append(f'{indent}""")')

      new_body = '\n'.join(out)
      new_src = src[:start + len(start_marker)] + new_body + src[start + len(start_marker) + end_idx + 1:]
      open(src_path, 'w').write(new_src)

  For the "chains of screens" idea you mentioned earlier — I won't apply it without your say-so given how the last attempt landed. If you do want it, two lighter-weight shapes I'd consider:

  1. Each say is one screen. Most of those screens are referenced from exactly one place anyway, so the id
  is dead weight.
  2. A vararg chain(prefix, """…""", """…""") in the strings block for sequential narration that genuinely is a numbered list (auto-named prefix.0, .1, …). No per-screen tags. Only useful when the scene plays the chain by index.

      579 +// ---- Colors ---------------------------------------------------------------                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
      580 +//                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      581 +// The legacy texts had inline ANSI byte sequences (e.g. `[31m...[37m`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
      582 +// We expose them as values + wrapper functions instead so the data file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
      583 +// reads `${red("DIES!")}` or `${YELLOW}DAWN${GREEN}` rather than raw escape                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
      584 +// codes. The string the engine receives is identical -- just lexically                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
      585 +// nicer at the call site.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      586 +//                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      587 +//   * `red(s)` / `yellow(s)` / `green(s)` / `magenta(s)` -- wrap `s` in the                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
      588 +//     color and reset to white (the most common pattern).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      589 +//                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      590 +//   * `RED` / `YELLOW` / `GREEN` / `MAGENTA` / `WHITE` -- bare color                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
      591 +//     switches. Use these when the legacy text resets to a non-default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
      592 +//     color (e.g. statusline yellow → green) or when the switch has no                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
      593 +//     pair (e.g. magenta HUNGRY hangs until next text).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
      594 +const val RED     = "[31m"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      595 +const val GREEN   = "[32m"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      596 +const val YELLOW  = "[33m"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      597 +const val MAGENTA = "[35m"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      598 +const val WHITE   = "[37m"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
      599 +                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
      600 +fun red(s: String):     String = "$RED$s$WHITE"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
      601 +fun green(s: String):   String = "$GREEN$s$WHITE"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
      602 +fun yellow(s: String):  String = "$YELLOW$s$WHITE"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      603 +fun magenta(s: String): String = "$MAGENTA$s$WHITE"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
      604 +                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
      605  // =============================================================================
      606  // SECTION 2 -- The full Rylween adventure.

      src_path = '/Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/full.dsl.kts'
      src = open(src_path).read()

      # Targeted replacements -- ordered most-specific to least-specific to avoid
      # clobbering. Each is a (literal-find, literal-replace) pair.
      subs = [
          # battle.monster.player_dies / melee_dies (str("...", "...DIES![37m"))

          ('            [37m<MORE>',                   '            ${WHITE}<MORE>'),

          ('            [31mCONGRATULATIONS![37m',     '            ${red("CONGRATULATIONS!")}'),

      count = 0

          else:
              print(f'NOT FOUND: {old[:60]!r}')

      open(src_path, 'w').write(src)
      print(f'replaced {count}/{len(subs)} ANSI occurrences')
      PYEOF

⏺ Done. Three samples landed for you to compare:

  1. Colors — red(), yellow(), green(), magenta() wrapper functions and bare RED/YELLOW/GREEN/MAGENTA/WHITE constants for the cases that reset to a non-default color (statusline) or just switch and hang (<MORE>, HUNGRY). 13 ANSI usages converted. Examples now read:

  str("battle.monster.player_dies", "${red("{target_name} DIES!")}")
  str("driv.statusline.time.dawn", "TIME: ${YELLOW}DAWN${GREEN}      ")

  2. Option 1 — inline narration at scene (scenes { scene("lute_chamber") { ... } }, around line 5717): The 11 lute-chamber narration screens that were declared in the strings block as str(...) and then referenced from the scene by screen("dungeon.lute_chamber.altar") etc. — all gone. The text is now in the scene
  body as chain("""...""" blocks interspersed with the encounters. Reads top-to-bottom like a screenplay. The 11 str() entries in the strings block are deleted.

  3. Option 2 — chain(prefix, ...) in strings block (around line 4002 + the borin_meet mission): The 6 borin_meet narration screens are now one chain("missions.borin_meet", """...""", """...""", ...) declaration. The mission body reduced from 6 screen(...) calls to one playChain("missions.borin_meet") call.

  Tradeoff between Option 1 and Option 2: Option 1 wins when narration is unique to one scene and interspersed with engine calls (encounters, mutations, etc.) — the screenplay flow is right there. Option 2 wins when the same narrative chain might be invoked from multiple places, or when you want narration to live
  in the strings block (alongside other text data) but still avoid per-screen ids.

  Take a look at lute_chamber (~line 5717) and borin_meet (mission ~6161 + strings ~4002) and let me know if either feels right to apply more broadly. File is 6462 lines.

⏺ Good catch — the transitions are a default and I never documented them. Let me make them explicit and configurable.                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  The default chain(""" a """, """ b """) between two blocks is waitInput + clw — emit block A, wait for the player to press a key, clear the text window, emit block B, wait, clear. Same as the legacy screen("id") semantics. I just hid it behind the chain() name without telling you.                                
   
  Three real patterns appear in the legacy data, and they should all be expressible:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  1. waitInput between blocks (default — most narration)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  2. pause N ms between blocks (cinematic / dramatic timing — e.g. ydarg confrontation's pause(2000) after door slams)                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  3. no clw between blocks (text accumulates in window — e.g. holy handgrenade's "Three. Four. ... FIVE.")                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  Let me update the DSL with named params and a comment, then show what lute_chamber would look like with explicit transitions where they matter.

⏺ So the answers, with the doc now in the framework (around line 195):             
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  Default for chain(""" a """, """ b """, """ c """): between every pair of blocks, and after the last one — emit, wait for the player to press a key, then clear the text window. Identical to chaining screen("a"); screen("b"); screen("c") in the legacy form.                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  Configure with named params on the same call:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  // Cinematic — N ms pause between blocks, no key-press required.
  chain(                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
      """ Suddenly there is an ear-splitting bang """,
      """ ...and silence falls. """,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      pauseMs = 1500,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  )                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
  // Text accumulates in the window — no clw between blocks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
  // Useful for stacking lines like a screen-fill.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  chain(                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
      """ Three. """,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
      """ Four. """,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      """ ...FIVE. """,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
      pauseMs = 800,                     
      clearBetween = false,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
  )
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
  // Both apply to all gaps.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
                                         
  Same params on the strings-block form: playChain("missions.borin_meet", pauseMs = 1500).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
  
  So in lute_chamber (line ~5717), every gap is a default-style "press key, clear, next" because that's what the original game did. If you want to make any of those gaps cinematic instead, add pauseMs = N to that chain block.

  ⎿  Wrote 268 lines to /Users/marcus/src/rylween-raw/dsl-improvements.md
        1 # DSL improvements -- typing pass                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
        2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
        3 A plan for tightening up `full.dsl.kts`. The DSL works, but most cross-references                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
        4 go through strings: scene names, monster slugs, item slugs, engine function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
        5 names, member field names, flag values. This works for the engine (which reads                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
        6 slugs at the bottom) but it's not very Kotlin-idiomatic, gives up IDE rename                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
        7 support, and lets typos slide to runtime.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
        8                                
        9 This document is an audit, a set of proposed patterns, and a phasing plan.
       10 Two patterns are sketched as experiments in the file already; the rest are
       11 on a roadmap.
       12
       13 ## What's currently string-typed
       14
       15 | Site | Example | Why it's a string today |
       16 |------|---------|-------------------------|
       17 | Engine calls | `engineCall("clw")`, `engineInt("rumour_roll")`, `engineCheck("inv_full")` | Generic shape: any engine fn -> string + args |
       18 | Member field writes | `member.setField("hit_points", v)` | One catch-all setter |
       19 | Member field reads | `member.hp`, `member.maxHp` already typed (good) | Mixed -- some typed, some not |
       20 | Bound bindings | `letBound("name", "pa_name", who)` + `say("Hello {name}")` | Slug ties the bind to the placeholder; both sides string |
       21 | Mutations | `mutate("gold", "sub", value)`, `mutate("priest_bonus", "add", ...)` | Generic catch-all |
       22 | Flag set/cmp | `flag("garth.bandits") set "recovered"` | State name is a string |
       23 | Cross-refs | `runScene("smith.buy")`, `enterDungeon("...")`, `give("torch")`, `cast("priest.heal")`, `encounter("orc")` | Slug -> slug |
       24 | Text ids | `screen("dungeon.foo")`, `text("...")` | Slug into strings table |
       25 | Bindings to scenes | `bindings("dx5" to "dx_str:5")` (mission-side) | String key + string DSL |
       26
       27 ## What we want
       28
       29 1. **Type-safety where it's free or cheap.** Member fields, primitive engine
       30    calls, well-known enumerations (pronoun kinds, ranges, tiers).
       31 2. **Stay loose at the engine boundary.** The serialized form the engine
       32    consumes is still slugs + ids. Typing happens in the DSL layer; one
       33    transform pass collapses to slugs.
       34 3. **Less DSL boilerplate, not more.** A typed wrapper that costs more
       35    characters than the string it replaces is a regression.
       36 4. **No two-pass evaluation tricks.** Forward references between data
       37    declarations (item -> scene -> mission) stay as slugs; trying to make
       38    them all `val` references requires lazy delegates and ordering games
       39    that aren't worth it.
       40
       41 ## Patterns to apply
       42
       43 ### Pattern A -- typed member field writes (experiment 1)
       44
       45 **Before:**
       46
       47 ```kotlin
       48 state.member(who).setField("hit_points", state.member(who).maxHp)
       49 state.member(who).setField("dead", 0)
       50 state.member(who).setField("magic", state.member(who).wis)
       51 ```
       52
       53 **After:**
       54
       55 ```kotlin
       56 val m = state.member(who)
       57 m.hp set m.maxHp
       58 m.dead set false
       59 m.mp set m.wis
       60 ```
       61
       62 `MemberRef.hp/mp/dead/...` already exist as `IntExpr` for reads. Make them
       63 `IntField` (subclass of `IntExpr`) that also supports `+=`, `-=`, and
       64 `set`. Booleans get a `BoolField` with `set true / set false`.
       65
       66 The legacy `setField("name", value)` stays as an escape hatch for fields we
       67 haven't promoted yet, but every named field on `MemberRef` becomes typed.
       68
       69 Cost: ~40 lines of DSL framework. Removes ~80 string-tagged setField calls
       70 across scenes. Strong win.
       71
       72 ### Pattern B -- typed binding via `bound()` (experiment 2)
       73
       74 **Before:**
       75
       76 ```kotlin
       77 letBound("name", "pa_name", who)
       78 letBound("pro_obj", "pronoun", who, "object")
       79 say("Hello {name}, {pro_obj} is here.")
       80 ```
       81
       82 The slug `"name"` has to match the placeholder `{name}` -- two strings, one
       83 intent. Renaming the binding requires touching both. The function name
       84 `"pa_name"` is also a string with no IDE knowledge.
       85
       86 **After:**
       87
       88 ```kotlin
       89 val name    = bound("name",    paName(who))
       90 val proObj  = bound("pro_obj", pronoun(who, OBJECT))
       91 say("Hello $name, $proObj is here.")
       92 ```
       93
       94 `paName(who: IntExpr): BoundExpr` returns a typed binding expression.
       95 `bound(slug, expr): String` records the binding for the engine and
       96 returns the placeholder string `"{slug}"`. Kotlin's normal string
       97 interpolation produces `"Hello {name}, {pro_obj} is here."` -- exactly
       98 what the engine expects.
       99
      100 Now `name` and `proObj` are real Kotlin references. Rename refactor works.
      101 The function `paName(...)` is type-checked. The slug still appears once
      102 (in the `bound(...)` call); future iteration could auto-generate slugs to
      103 remove it entirely.
      104
      105 Engine function shells we'd add:
      106
      107 ```kotlin
      108 fun paName(idx: IntExpr): BoundExpr
      109 fun pronoun(idx: IntExpr, kind: PronounKind): BoundExpr
      110 fun objectName(itemId: IntExpr): BoundExpr
      111 fun resEnum(table: String, key: IntExpr): BoundExpr
      112 fun resEnumNameBySym(table: String, sym: String): BoundExpr
      113 fun resNpcRole(role: String): BoundExpr
      114 fun npcNameAtRole(role: String): BoundExpr
      115 fun npcLocAtRole(role: String): BoundExpr
      116 fun wldLocationX(name: String): BoundExpr
      117 fun wldLocationY(name: String): BoundExpr
      118
      119 enum class PronounKind { SUBJECT, OBJECT, POSSESSIVE }
      120 ```
      121
      122 Cost: ~30 lines of framework + the enum. Removes ~60 `letBound("...", "fn",
      123 args)` calls across scenes; each becomes more typed and shorter.
      124
      125 ### Pattern C -- typed flag state machines (later)
      126
      127 **Before:**
      128
      129 ```kotlin
      130 flag("garth.bandits") set "recovered"
      131 on(flag("garth.bandits") eq "accepted") { ... }
      132 ```
      133
      134 **After:**
      135
      136 ```kotlin
      137 val GarthBandits = flagDecl("garth.bandits",
      138     "none", "accepted", "recovered", "closed")
      139
      140 GarthBandits set GarthBandits.recovered
      141 on(GarthBandits eq GarthBandits.accepted) { ... }
      142 ```
      143
      144 `flagDecl(slug, vararg states)` returns a typed object with one property
      145 per state value. State references are typed. Invalid states fail to
      146 compile. The IDE autocompletes valid transitions.
      147
      148 Cost: real boilerplate -- 13 flag declarations need to be turned into
      149 typed handles, each used 3-12 times. The `state { flag(...) }` block
      150 already declares states; we'd promote that block from declarations to
      151 real Kotlin properties.
      152
      153 Not done yet. Worth doing in a follow-up; pattern is clear, time isn't.
      154
      155 ### Pattern D -- typed cross-refs (deferred / probably skip)
      156
      157 **Before:**
      158
      159 ```kotlin
      160 encounter("orc", mandatory = true)
      161 give("torch")
      162 runScene("smith.buy")
      163 enterDungeon("fire_shield_cave")
      164 cast("priest.heal")
      165 ```
      166
      167 **After (one option):**
      168
      169 ```kotlin
      170 val torch  by item("torch") { ... }
      171 val orc    by monster("orc") { ... }
      172 val smithBuy by scene("smith.buy") { ... }
      173
      174 scene("dungeon_x") {
      175     encounter(orc, mandatory = true)
      176     give(torch)
      177     runScene(smithBuy)
      178 }
      179 ```
      180
      181 This requires lazy property delegates, two-pass evaluation, and ordering
      182 discipline (you can't reference `torch` until its `val` line has run).
      183
      184 The win is small: Kotlin already lets you Cmd-click a string slug if your
      185 IDE indexes the project. Slugs are concise. The DSL stays declarative.
      186
      187 **Recommendation: don't do this.** Slugs are fine for cross-refs. Spend
      188 the typing budget on Patterns A and B, where the gain per change is
      189 larger.
      190
      191 ### Pattern E -- typed engine call shells (selective)
      192
      193 The catch-all `engineCall("name", args...)` is fine for one-off engine
      194 hooks. Where the same engine call appears 5+ times across scenes, promote
      195 it to a typed shell:
      196
      197 ```kotlin
      198 fun Script.statusLine() = engineCall("status_line")
      199 fun Script.inventoryList() = engineCall("inv_list")
      200 fun Script.advanceHour(amount: IntExpr) = engineCall("advance_hour", amount)
      201 fun Script.invFull(): Cond = engineCheck("inv_full")
      202 fun Script.partyMemberMax(): IntExpr = engineInt("pa_party_member_max")  // already done
      203 ```
      204
      205 Some of these already exist (`statusLine()`, `clw()`). Audit the call
      206 sites and promote any engine hook used >=5x. Goal: typo-resistant
      207 helpers; the rest stay generic. Cost: trivial; just collect the helpers.
      208
      209 ## What stays string
      210
      211 The engine boundary. By the time the structure leaves the DSL and reaches
      212 the engine, every cross-ref is a slug or text id. The translation lives
      213 in one well-defined transform pass (DSL -> world model -> engine view).
      214
      215 Specifically:
      216 - text ids in `screen("...")` and `text("...")`
      217 - emitIndexed format strings (`"speak.lodge.j{}"`)
      218 - text-template placeholders (`{name}`, `{pro_obj}`) -- the engine still
      219   reads these from the template at emit time, even when the placeholder
      220   was generated by a `bound()` call
      221
      222 Don't try to make the engine boundary itself typed. It's a serialization
      223 contract.
      224
      225 ## Roadmap
      226
      227 | Phase | Pattern | Cost | Win |
      228 |-------|---------|------|-----|
      229 | 1a    | A: typed member field writes | low  | ~80 sites cleaner |
      230 | 1b    | B: typed `bound()` helpers   | low  | ~60 sites cleaner |
      231 | 2a    | E: typed engine call shells (audit + promote) | low | typo-resistance |
      232 | 2b    | C: typed flag state machines | medium | every flag site cleaner |
      233 | 3     | D: typed cross-refs           | high | small gain; recommend skip |
      234
      235 ## Auto-slug as a future step
      236
      237 In Pattern B, the slug `"m3_name"` in `bound("m3_name", paName(3))` is
      238 internal -- the engine uses it as a placeholder key but the data writer
      239 doesn't care what string it is. We can auto-generate:
      240
      241 ```kotlin
      242 val name = bound(paName(3))     // returns "{__b0}" or similar
      243 val pron = bound(pronoun(3, OBJECT))   // returns "{__b1}"
      244 say("$name hears $pron!")
      245 ```
      246
      247 The Kotlin string interpolation still produces a literal placeholder; the
      248 engine gets a unique generated key. Caller only types the typed expression.
      249
      250 This is a follow-up to Phase 1b; needs care around scoping (each Script
      251 body has its own counter; don't collide across nested scripts).
      252
      253 ## Experiments shipped in this branch
      254
      255 `full.dsl.kts` already contains:
      256
      257 - **Experiment 1 (Pattern A)**: `MemberRef.hp/mp/dead/...` are now writable
      258   via typed property fields. The `church.heal` scene was rewritten to use
      259   `m.hp set m.maxHp` etc. Old `setField("name", value)` still works for
      260   fields not yet promoted.
      261
      262 - **Experiment 2 (Pattern B)**: `bound()` and `paName/pronoun/...` engine
      263   shells added. The `lute_chamber` scene was rewritten to use them. The
      264   `silver_sanctum` scene was rewritten to demonstrate the chained
      265   bindings (`mt_slot` then `mt_name` resolved through the bound slot).
      266
      267 Look at those scenes for a side-by-side feel; the rest of the file is
      268 untouched so nothing else breaks.

  machines, typed cross-refs, typed engine-call shells), tradeoffs, and a phased roadmap. Recommendation: do A and B now, B+E next, defer
   C, skip D.

  full.dsl.kts (6576 lines) with two experiments shipped:

  Experiment 1 — typed member field writes (Pattern A). New IntField and BoolField types. MemberRef.hp/mp/dead/etc are now typed handles
  supporting +=, -=, set. The old setField(name, value) stays as an escape hatch.

  In church.heal (~line 4805):
  val m = state.member(who)
  on(m.hp eq m.maxHp) { ... }
  m.hp set m.maxHp                 // was: m.setField("hit_points", m.maxHp)

  Experiment 2 — typed bindings via bound() (Pattern B). New BoundExpr class + helpers (paName, pronoun, objectName, resEnum, resNpcRole,
   npcNameAtRole, wldLocationX/Y, etc.) and a PronounKind enum. The bound(slug, expr) function records the binding and returns the
  placeholder "{slug}" so Kotlin string interpolation just works.

  In lute_chamber (~line 5824):
  val m3Name    = bound("m3_name",    paName(3))
  val m3Pronoun = bound("m3_pronoun", pronoun(3, PronounKind.OBJECT))
  cinematic("""
      $m3Name suddenly
      hears something behind
      $m3Pronoun!
  """, ...)

  In silver_sanctum (~line 5726) the chained-binding case:
  val mtSlot = bound("mt_slot", resNpcRole("master_thief"))
  val mtName = bound("mt_name", resEnum("name", v("mt_slot")))

  Both experiments are scoped — old call sites elsewhere (letBound, setField) still compile and work. The DSL accepts both shapes during
  the transition.

  Take a look at the three converted scenes (church.heal, lute_chamber, silver_sanctum) and the plan doc; let me know if the typed shape
  feels right and I'll roll out broader.
